and demand corporations pay up for using a global pandemic to increase

their wealth on the backs of poor and working class people") [Click here to demand Congress pass a windfall profits penalty and demand corporations pay up for using a global pandemic to increase their wealth on the backs of poor and working class people](https://www.cornelwest2024.com/organizedgreed?e=2c4ab4fbefc09c0d9c12f8df438b31c5&utm_source=cornelwest&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=20240125organized_greed&n=2)
---
My Dear and Precious Siblings, You are well aware of how my Christian faith and the teachings of my revolutionary savior, Jesus Christ, guide and inform my values, my morality, and my politics. To that end, not much makes me more indignant than witnessing oligarchs and their sycophants take advantage of, and extract from poor and working class folk to increase their wealth at the expense of the most vulnerable. It’s why Jesus went into that temple, and it’s why I write to you today. Last week our friends at the think tank, Groundwork Collaborative, released a report proving that 53% of inflation, the highest level in 40 years, during the height of the COVID pandemic was driven by the organized greed of corporations. The practice was so iniquitous the report’s authors even coined the phrase “greedflation” to fully accentuate such a sinister scheme. How else can you describe the fact that CEO’s literally bragged to their stockholders about keeping prices high for consumers even though corporate input costs decreased all in the name of widening profit margins? **It’s time to dismantle the organized greed of corporate cartels and the derelict duopoly who continue to place profits over people.[Click here to demand Congress immediately pass a Windfall Profits Penalty so we can get that money back in the hands of poor and working class people. ](https://www.cornelwest2024.com/organizedgreed?e=2c4ab4fbefc09c0d9c12f8df438b31c5&utm_source=cornelwest&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=20240125organized_greed&n=3)**
---
[ ](https://www.cornelwest2024.com/organizedgreed?e=2c4ab4fbefc09c0d9c12f8df438b31c5&utm_source=cornelwest&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=20240125organized_greed&n=4)
---
We know that we can’t rely on the derelict duopoly to do the right thing and stand with the people without pressure. President Obama and the Democrats had their chance to bring these Wall Street vultures to justice in 2008, but instead rewarded them with a bailout using the people’s money when so many were still reeling from the worst financial collapse since the Great Depression. And ten years later, Trump and the Republicans rewarded these same money hungry miscreants with a massive tax break on the backs of poor and working class people, many of whom are paying a higher tax rate than CEOs like Warren Buffett and Jeff Bezos. This is nothing more than crack pipe capitalism - the addicts of avarice continue to achieve although they deceive. This must end, and it must end right now. [**Please sign our campaign’s petition demanding Congress seize at least 70% of corporate windfall profits and redistribute these funds to poor and working class people.**](https://www.cornelwest2024.com/organizedgreed?e=2c4ab4fbefc09c0d9c12f8df438b31c5&utm_source=cornelwest&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=20240125organized_greed&n=5) With your help we can take back what is rightfully ours and send a message that, moving forward, corporations who use disaster to benefit themselves will have to pay the price so the people don’t shoulder the costs of organized greed. With Love Supreme, Dr. Cornel West
---

Hi friend, it’s Senator Tammy Baldwin. I know better than anyone that winning in Wisconsin isn’t easy — our state is home to some of the closest races in the nation, and this November will be no different.
I’ve already been named one of the most vulnerable U.S. Senate incumbents on the ballot — and Republicans are gearing up to spend a fortune to flip my seat red.
We’ve got a tough fight ahead of us, and it’s going to take a lot of time and resources to build the grassroots coalition we’ll need to win big in November.
I know this team has what it takes to beat right-wing mega-donors at their own game (we’ve done it before!) but it’s going to take all of us working together, which is why I’m asking: Can you split a donation between my reelection campaign and the Wisconsin Senate Democrats today? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ssdc-split-baldwin?refcode=gcemail]

That’s why it’s so important that we support the WI Senate Dems year-round efforts to support candidates who are committed to defending democracy and winning a pro-choice majority.
It’s going to take a broad grassroots coalition to support Democrats running in tough districts in 2024 and beyond. Friend, will you split a contribution with the WI Senate Dems to help us keep Wisconsin blue this November? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ssdc-split-baldwin?refcode=gcemail]

_**To Make Health Care Affordable, Give Patients Choices**_ By Bobby Jindal & Heidi Overton
---
Affordability is on the mind of every American in 2024. From groceries to gas, Americans are spending more. Health care is no different, especially for those with costly medical conditions and high deductibles who started back at $0 of their "deductible met" on January 1.

Health care affordability was recently listed as a top issue for voters in 2024 alongside inflation, with eight in ten and nine in ten wanting presidential candidates to talk about the issues, respectively. In 2023, family health insurance premiums rose to nearly $24,000—a 7 percent increase from 2022—and one in five adults with insurance reported not obtaining needed health care in the past year due to cost.

The country is also spending more overall. Every December, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services provides national health expenditure data for the prior year. Last month's data showed that in 2022, Americans spent $4.5 trillion—17.3 percent of our GDP—on health care. This was a 4.1 percent increase from 2021 and averaged about $13,500 per person. **[FINISH READING ON NEWSWEEK.COM](http://links.americanxt.com/u/click?_t=45ea7b9dcedb45198104e7ca02a78270&_m=f32e20f920784528b016506203614a29&_e=VfcyrYdacEX4KFBwvWzm_aOZgBsbDMixZ2Q_lRGhPlve9UyygstMW5pQ2t-gOoFWsten8uaywo8dyobuGWpeG4qGAR7ZoJdz6XC7Hh803uu8To8HqXTyl_F_CK1DAlxu1G2SDZe3qbBup99mbMnojmO-BRNeUyhI8sdAcqHc8_ZSKCu57j7mZc3HDz63O2bPOxz5hxuOlb5p9XFTNuBYWkYyitg-3USNDdaQ2JwkGwzv3UY_X8GCBVa3FaBHDTRonkXTUTKVIyx4-96l-S2FmYH47D4IDq5Mgy8GAyHIgD4%3D)**

body:
| | | | |
---
**John Teichert Announces Historic Fundraising for U.S. Senate Race**
**BALTIMORE, Md.** – Today, retired Brigadier General John Teichert announced that his campaign raised $304,000 during the fourth quarter of 2023.
It’s a historic fundraising haul for Teichert, a first-time candidate for any political office who announced his bid for the open U.S. Senate seat in Maryland back in October. Teichert’s fundraising feat is the largest amount raised in the first quarter by any GOP candidate who went on to become the party’s nominee since former Lieutenant Governor Michael Steele in 2006.
More importantly, his fundraising success is a strong sign of a broad-based grassroots backing of his campaign, with approximately 95 percent of Teichert’s donations coming from low-dollar donors, Teichert received support from across the state of Maryland. Donations for Teichert’s campaign came in from 22 of Maryland’s 23 counties and Baltimore City.
Responding to the fundraising success he’s received since his campaign began, General Teichert released the following statement:
**“I am overwhelmed with gratitude for the wide swath of Marylanders who have embraced my commitment as a new kind of candidate – one dedicated to leadership, not politics,”** Teichert said in the statement. **“Our historic fundraising success is yet another sign that Marylanders are ready for change not just here in the state, but in Washington D.C. as well. I look forward to hearing more from the people of our great state as I travel extensively to earn their support and ultimately serve and represent them in the U.S. Senate.”**
Teichert’s historic fundraising comes on the heels of support from law enforcement officers, state delegates and senators, and other former Maryland elected officials, including former Lt. Governor Rutherford.

name: John Kasich
subject: This is a losing strategy
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kasich for America, not authorized by any
body:
What's the harm in letting the voters decide who they want as their candidate?| | | [](http://links.johnkasich.com/u/click?_t=6a3b28686d0a4d77958e12349305a4fe&_m=cdbe0e446ea8426c8fa9217f44127e8b&_e=6ZVcqW9u6ydRUi3AYFTQjiIN0Hf6eiqVTl9Su8f-jXr3hJfjOzzp0hFKD0oEzgnF5utGwmN2vR-CefHXXlDE8w_03ZYzOctQrQ9NGcwcJYsxnEAy2dPXLtFIk9Fji2OEiaFX0cxYOeEoJZoapuH7THv15WF7WEvM4O3SbLJYeZcx4Sz-vgtD6FRqlRmOCxGZJFzgJbNVJaRsQFxXFTQykQ%3D%3D)
---
Peter, While there is no doubt that Donald Trump won the Iowa Caucus and New Hampshire Primary, I am alarmed at how quickly people have rushed to declare him the nominee and put enormous pressure on Nikki Haley to drop out.

Even the chairwoman of the Republican National Committee joined the chorus. Shouldn't the RNC remain neutral in primary elections? What's the point in even having a primary if we're just going to let a bunch of pundits and DC insiders decide who the Republican nominee should be?

**My question is this:** What's the harm in letting the voters decide who they want as their candidate?

In total, fewer than 450,000 people participated in the Iowa Caucus and New Hampshire Primary. In 2016, there were more than 31 million votes cast in the GOP primaries.

In light of this, I can understand the frustration Nikki Haley and her team are feeling right now. She has every right to stay in the race until such time as she feels it is the best thing for the party and for the country to suspend her campaign.

When I ran for president in 2016, people told me to drop out also because it benefited them if I did that. But we had a sophisticated delegate operation and we knew we had a narrow, but viable path to win at a contested convention when bound delegates could abandon Trump and vote for me instead on the second ballot.

When it became clear that that was no longer possible, I ended my candidacy because I owed it to my donors and supporters since a path didn't exist anymore.

**Rather than seeing primary elections as a threat, party leaders should see them as something to be celebrated as our candidates debate the issues that our party can rally around and use to build coalitions of voters for the general election**.

We have serious challenges right now in America and we owe it to future generations to solve them - not kick the can down the road. By skipping the primary and just anointing a deeply flawed candidate, we are dramatically increasing the chances of another big Democrat win.

clean_body: What's the harm in letting the voters decide who they want as their candidate?| | | Peter, While there is no doubt that Donald Trump won the Iowa Caucus and New Hampshire Primary, I am alarmed at how quickly people have rushed to declare him the nominee and put enormous pressure on Nikki Haley to drop out. Even the chairwoman of the Republican National Committee joined the chorus. Shouldn't the RNC remain neutral in primary elections? What's the point in even having a primary if we're just going to let a bunch of pundits and DC insiders decide who the Republican nominee should be? My question is this: What's the harm in letting the voters decide who they want as their candidate? In total, fewer than 450,000 people participated in the Iowa Caucus and New Hampshire Primary. In 2016, there were more than 31 million votes cast in the GOP primaries. In light of this, I can understand the frustration Nikki Haley and her team are feeling right now. She has every right to stay in the race until such time as she feels it is the best thing for the party and for the country to suspend her campaign. When I ran for president in 2016, people told me to drop out also because it benefited them if I did that. But we had a sophisticated delegate operation and we knew we had a narrow, but viable path to win at a contested convention when bound delegates could abandon Trump and vote for me instead on the second ballot. When it became clear that that was no longer possible, I ended my candidacy because I owed it to my donors and supporters since a path didn't exist anymore. Rather than seeing primary elections as a threat, party leaders should see them as something to be celebrated as our candidates debate the issues that our party can rally around and use to build coalitions of voters for the general election. We have serious challenges right now in America and we owe it to future generations to solve them - not kick the can down the road. By skipping the primary and just anointing a deeply flawed candidate, we are dramatically increasing the chances of another big Democrat win. With Trump at the helm, Republicans lost in 2018, 2020, 2021 and 2022. Why in the world would they think that this time around will be any different? clean_body: | This week a report in JAMA [Journal of the American Medical Association] Internal Medicine estimated the damage done by the Dobbs decision overturning a woman’s right to control her own body. Since Dobbs , nearly 65,000 rapes have resulted in obviously unwanted pregnancies in the 14 states that outlawed abortion. Worse, most of those states have made it impossible to know whether these women were able to get an abortion after their rapes. I am the son of a strong and brilliant woman, the husband of a strong and brilliant woman, and the father of two strong and brilliant women. It is simply unacceptable that politicians can obliterate their rights of bodily autonomy and privacy. = | | = As if the JAMA numbers aren’t bad enough, the American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology estimates that only 5% of rapes result in pregnancy. This means that women in the 14 states that have outlawed abortion are likely suffering an epidemic of about 1.3 million rapes in less than two years. Yet Scott Perry voted against the Violence Against Women Act. And even though pregnancies resulting from rape result in higher rates of domestic violence and poverty, Scott Perry voted against the Child Care Tax Credits that lift children and families out of poverty. Scott Perry is a continuing threat to women’s and children’s freedom and safety. Sadly, all of this was predictable as soon as Donald Trump appointed three extreme justices to the Supreme Court. = | = Thank you. – Rick | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Friends of Rick Coplen | =

name: Zach Shrewsbury
subject: Our healthcare needs a revolution
body:
| | | [ ](https://www.shrewsburyforsenate.com/r?u=sTrCoaT-YmDhY88aC-xe_4EuiRHvEQu_OzjBiZlAGzs2u921EReiR88ARqrt5HWpbBPunnEofCMh9dr_AFzKQYWEKwMnXHQHR7lJnt56395dz4Ig8HBG3941H3HiQxD8&e=835c7faa13004566534194ac192acb50&utm_source=shrewsburyforsenate&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=012524_healthcare&n=1&v=18)
---
Dear Friend, Almost every day, I'm reminded of how Congress puts corporate profits over the interests of the people it represents. A prime example is our healthcare system. Despite our nation's vast expenditure on healthcare, our health outcomes lag far behind other developed countries, and our life expectancy is declining.
---
[ ](https://www.shrewsburyforsenate.com/r?u=sTrCoaT-YmDhY88aC-xe_4EuiRHvEQu_OzjBiZlAGzs2u921EReiR88ARqrt5HWpbBPunnEofCMh9dr_AFzKQYWEKwMnXHQHR7lJnt56395dz4Ig8HBG3941H3HiQxD8&e=835c7faa13004566534194ac192acb50&utm_source=shrewsburyforsenate&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=012524_healthcare&n=2&v=18)
---
While the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare) made strides in expanding health insurance coverage, the truth remains stark: many still struggle with high premiums, deductibles, and out-of-pocket expenses. The true winners of the policy shift with ACA are insurance companies and big Pharma. In West Virginia, almost 15 percent of adults cannot afford necessary medical care, and 20 percent lack a primary physician. This is more than a statistic; it's a crisis impacting real lives, leading to premature deaths from chronic conditions like diabetes, cancer, and heart disease. I am committed to changing this narrative. That's why I am a staunch advocate for a universal, single-payer-type healthcare system as proposed in the Medicare for All Act. **[Join our campaign if you want a champion for Medicare for All in the Senate.](https://www.shrewsburyforsenate.com/r?u=sTrCoaT-YmDhY88aC-xe_4EuiRHvEQu_OzjBiZlAGzs2u921EReiR88ARqrt5HWpbBPunnEofCMh9dr_AFzKQYWEKwMnXHQHR7lJnt56395dz4Ig8HBG3941H3HiQxD8&e=835c7faa13004566534194ac192acb50&utm_source=shrewsburyforsenate&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=012524_healthcare&n=3&v=18)**
---
| [](https://www.shrewsburyforsenate.com/r?u=sTrCoaT-YmDhY88aC-xe_4EuiRHvEQu_OzjBiZlAGzs2u921EReiR88ARqrt5HWpbBPunnEofCMh9dr_AFzKQYWEKwMnXHQHR7lJnt56395dz4Ig8HBG3941H3HiQxD8&e=835c7faa13004566534194ac192acb50&utm_source=shrewsburyforsenate&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=012524_healthcare&n=4&v=18 "DONATE") [DONATE](https://www.shrewsburyforsenate.com/r?u=sTrCoaT-YmDhY88aC-xe_4EuiRHvEQu_OzjBiZlAGzs2u921EReiR88ARqrt5HWpbBPunnEofCMh9dr_AFzKQYWEKwMnXHQHR7lJnt56395dz4Ig8HBG3941H3HiQxD8&e=835c7faa13004566534194ac192acb50&utm_source=shrewsburyforsenate&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=012524_healthcare&n=4&v=18)
---
This transformative plan guarantees comprehensive medical, dental, and mental health care without the burden of premiums, deductibles, or out-of-pocket costs. Imagine a system where prescription drugs are affordable, mirroring the models of Canada and countries of the European Union, funded through progressive equitable taxes and the elimination of inefficiencies, corporate fraud, and profiteering in our current healthcare system. The journey to pass the Medicare for All Act is challenging. We are up against formidable opponents: the health insurance and pharmaceutical industries, armed with legions of lobbyists. However, history has shown us that powerful industries can be overcome. From civil rights to environmental laws, change has always been driven by people uniting for a common cause. I pledge to be your voice when elected to the U.S. Senate, relentlessly advocating for the Medicare for All Act. But I cannot do this alone. Your support is crucial. clean_body: | | | Dear Friend, Almost every day, I'm reminded of how Congress puts corporate profits over the interests of the people it represents. A prime example is our healthcare system. Despite our nation's vast expenditure on healthcare, our health outcomes lag far behind other developed countries, and our life expectancy is declining. While the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare) made strides in expanding health insurance coverage, the truth remains stark: many still struggle with high premiums, deductibles, and out-of-pocket expenses. The true winners of the policy shift with ACA are insurance companies and big Pharma. In West Virginia, almost 15 percent of adults cannot afford necessary medical care, and 20 percent lack a primary physician. This is more than a statistic; it's a crisis impacting real lives, leading to premature deaths from chronic conditions like diabetes, cancer, and heart disease. I am committed to changing this narrative. That's why I am a staunch advocate for a universal, single-payer-type healthcare system as proposed in the Medicare for All Act. | "DONATE" This transformative plan guarantees comprehensive medical, dental, and mental health care without the burden of premiums, deductibles, or out-of-pocket costs. Imagine a system where prescription drugs are affordable, mirroring the models of Canada and countries of the European Union, funded through progressive equitable taxes and the elimination of inefficiencies, corporate fraud, and profiteering in our current healthcare system. The journey to pass the Medicare for All Act is challenging. We are up against formidable opponents: the health insurance and pharmaceutical industries, armed with legions of lobbyists. However, history has shown us that powerful industries can be overcome. From civil rights to environmental laws, change has always been driven by people uniting for a common cause. I pledge to be your voice when elected to the U.S. Senate, relentlessly advocating for the Medicare for All Act. But I cannot do this alone. Your support is crucial. Together, we can make history. body:
Congress shall make no law “abridging the freedom of speech.”

|
---
| | | **Congress shall make no law “abridging the freedom of speech.”
**
---
---
[](https://www.kennedy24.com/donate?e=d33e868971601c1c714cfe0555abd394&utm_source=joinkennedy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=censor_1_25_24_email_1_1_nd&n=1)
|
---
Dear Peter,
Our outrage that the Canadian Supreme Court would force psychiatrist Jordan Peterson to undergo “social media training” for “demeaning posts”— __or lose his medical license__ —did not go unnoticed.
Even the popular Dr. Peterson himself thanked our campaign for highlighting his plight on his X account (formerly known as Twitter).
The fact is, we live in a country that was built upon the principles of freedom—spelled out in our Bill of Rights, the first 10 Amendments of our Constitution.
The First Amendment says in no uncertain terms: Congress shall make no law “abridging the freedom of speech.”
And while Canada does not share our Constitution, they have long held to the principles found therein.
Several media outlets were as shocked as we were that someone like Dr. Peterson could be forced to undergo training or lose his job.
One news headline read:
[](https://www.kennedy24.com/donate?e=d33e868971601c1c714cfe0555abd394&utm_source=joinkennedy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=censor_1_25_24_email_1_1_nd&n=2)
The article noted:
| A U.S. presidential candidate and a U.S. congressman have condemned recent Canadian court rulings that allow the College of Psychologists of Ontario (CPO) to require Jordan Peterson to undergo social media training in order to keep his professional licence.
---
Dr. Peterson, in a Jan. 20 post on X, shared a letter sent by Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s office to a recipient named "Norman" that noted similarities between Dr. Peterson's case and Mr. Kennedy's campaign, which the letter said is "currently facing mainstream media censorship."
"The breaking news that a Canadian Court is forcing psychiatrist Jordan Peterson to undergo state-sanctioned media training because of 'demeaning' social media posts is an assault to the fundamental tenets of Democracy and Freedom," said the letter, emailed to Mr. Kennedy's campaign supporters on Jan. 20, as confirmed by his press secretary, Stefanie Spear.
Mr. Kennedy, a former Democrat, had initially challenged U.S. President Joe Biden for the Democratic nomination. In October 2023, he announced he would run for president as an independent instead. The letter, which seeks additional support for his campaign, condemns authoritarianism while making reference to Dr. Peterson's case.
"That a Canadian court would force anyone to submit to their speech codes or else lose his or her ability to earn a living more resembles Communist-led China, not a free nation," it said.
"Authoritarianism was tried by many nations in the 20th century, and it failed every single time because people of the free world opposed those regimes that sought to terminate fundamental human rights."
###
Our nation has led the free nations of the world in protecting and promoting human rights. The United States has long served as a light for the world to emulate, and we have a long standing agreement with our Canadian friends on this critical issue.
Yet in today’s age, there are many—even in our own country—who are calling for more and more censorship.
According to one recent [poll](https://www.kennedy24.com/r?u=954wJVfXJnGDSMt_j90vIsrjhRXLT-nmcgjtW0sV489AefUIk-qAWJwKUxFmyMSZAb-2M8mFMJrGNZrtx2nMKrBq4AbHgcKJdaqrXIDPveiUedE0U2Uj2eQpqr_vWhpf8QwadpwaPPHSvAzDoj_xIg&e=d33e868971601c1c714cfe0555abd394&utm_source=joinkennedy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=censor_1_25_24_email_1_1_nd&n=3) in which respondents were asked if they agree or disagree with the statement “I disapprove of what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it”, only 31% of Democratic voters “strongly agreed” and only 34% of Independents agreed with the sentiment.

Why? Because the moment I was elected Speaker by my Republican colleagues, the Radical Left IMMEDIATELY unleashed a coordinated, preplanned political hit job against me.
* The Liberal Media spun up hit piece after hit piece to smear me in the press - Biden's former Press Secretary even attacked me for being a Christian on MSNBC.
* Politico fired off this headline: _" Democrats rev up the opposition machine against Mike Johnson."_
* And I can't even begin to tell you how many Democrat fundraising emails and texts I saw in the minutes following the final vote - I'm bracing myself for the next FEC reports.

Look:

These vicious attacks are a dime a dozen in Washington. They don't intimidate me. _But I 'll let you in on a little secret: that's not _really_ the goal..._

The _real_ goal of this political ambush is two-fold: **1)** smear the good names of every House Republican to hurt them electorally, and **2)** scare Liberals enough to whip out their credit cards, fill in their info, and donate to Democrats.

**It 's about power and money. Nothing else.**

That's why it's mission-critical that we stand up for ourselves in critical moments like this. _**[So as one of my first moves as Speaker, I'm teaming up with my fellow Louisianian - Majority Leader Steve Scalise - to set a goal of raising one million dollars between now and the end of the month.](http://links.greatamericatoday.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=69d92758de5840aa92dd319dfaf29f12&_e=QuVfY1TEuqhF8_SWSEk7zqXKwXuvgsPnRlEYdHc6ez80pnPNAS4xUDsVwZrDL0v0jbabdv5RPBZS1Bik5pMQpDrf3pKmkYnktwyXxeYc6taDY6Kk70NsvFxRCEJm6HcfuOBSk1FAXSKnjtl6SepNeSEKYEHL2ZmMmXHhhZTaWxOOnBObhOnbXiH9NzyA5ytFFU-CbcGnIba0z2PPkraxjGLEEc0FHhaf9j7dhMHp6HEvBmO9_qUCb086I2Xo3z36ZaGgWr7PVtrIIqo0pX24TMmeXpbUdmVuQdOx92acLHvRCUgkOb_psNgZ1nlrG5FvDh1WxvstXtw5ZNJNajV9biHyh99NFWFq_zQXR7VVIPQp3EKz0zX4VUaBl2wPS0XUKtiDvmN9q2YduI6WXE-4c3EzQ2-_z-jR5zEuyRCljaI%3D "So as one of my first moves as Speaker, I’m teaming up with my fellow Louisianian – Majority Leader Steve Scalise – to set a goal of raising one million dollars between now and the end of the month.")**_

It's ambitious. I get it. But that's the bare minimum we need to fully fund our campaign operations in battleground races across the country.

**If we fall short of that, we 'll be forced to SLASH our voter contact budgets, GUT our digital outreach efforts, and pull our ads OFF THE AIRWAVES. Nothing could be worse for our plans to defend and expand our slim House Majority.**

So here's my final pitch to you:

We urgently need your help. Not next week, not in the new year - right here and right now.

The difference between a strong Conservative Majority and one controlled by the Liberal Machine will come down to can't-miss fundraising goals just like this.

Let me make myself perfectly clear:

_I 'm not asking you to pitch in more than you can afford. If you can spare $50 or $100, I would be tremendously grateful. But if you can only spare $5 or $10, I would be equally appreciative._

_**[The ONLY thing I ask is for every Conservative in the country to chip in SOMETHING.](http://links.greatamericatoday.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=69d92758de5840aa92dd319dfaf29f12&_e=QuVfY1TEuqhF8_SWSEk7zqXKwXuvgsPnRlEYdHc6ez80pnPNAS4xUDsVwZrDL0v0jbabdv5RPBZS1Bik5pMQpDrf3pKmkYnktwyXxeYc6taDY6Kk70NsvFxRCEJm6HcfuOBSk1FAXSKnjtl6SepNeSEKYEHL2ZmMmXHhhZTaWxOOnBObhOnbXiH9NzyA5ytFFU-CbcGnIba0z2PPkraxjGLEEc0FHhaf9j7dhMHp6HEvBmO9_qUCb086I2Xo3z36ZaGgWr7PVtrIIqo0pX24TDzThDtq4kLn84CvDgfhpBMICHR3KZrDG8D1lyZMLlE5lLJngg3FNIpSMbD-LKBgxBu--X9D1gHT33rjQo95F6QL_dfBi_1pDC9gKrG6tPYC5dVx7yKtJEh-rMIYIjDi2npKJauBhFFjWjiFI9cL5EA%3D "The ONLY thing I ask is for every Conservative in the country to chip in SOMETHING.")**_

#
We’re Veterans. A lot of the people reading this are Veterans, too. Many more of you are members of Military Families. And even if you’re not in either of those groups, you’re a part of this team.
When you join the Military you swear an oath to defend the Constitution of the United States. We took that oath seriously.
And that's why we’re writing to you today. To put it very simply, our Constitution and our democracy are under greater threat today than at any point in our lifetimes.
Trump is doing everything he can to march back into the White House. If he takes back the presidency, he has stated openly that he would use the Military and the Department of Justice to crack down on his political opponents. He will gut the federal government and fill it with MAGA fanatics and loyalists. And that’s just what he and his team have said publicly. There is no telling how far he will go to turn the United States into a dictatorship.
We are steps away.
